ldx3 — Talks & Vendors

Conference talk notes and vendors-to-explore from LDX3.

Talks

  • 2026-06-03 · Engineering Leadership in 2026 · Scott (LeadDev)
    The Great Flattening is real but driven as much by pandemic over-hiring as AI; orgs are moving from 5-layer pyramids to 3-layer plateaus, squeezing middle management and pulling leaders back toward hands-on code.
  • 2026-06-03 · Platform Engineering for Developers, Architects, and the Rest of Us (AI Agents) · Daniel Bryant (Syntasso)
    AI increases demand for platforms; treat platform architecture with the same rigour as software architecture across three layers (App Choreography, Platform Orchestration, Infrastructure Orchestration) and manage resources as a fleet to serve humans and bounded agents alike.
  • 2026-06-03 · Reading the Game: Mental Skills for High-Performing Engineering Teams · Cathy
    Cathy's player-to-coach journey reframes engineering management through sports psychology — coach the mental state, build for resilience and autonomy, and practise a Visualise / Self-talk / Reset game plan.
  • 2026-06-03 · We Doubled Engineer Productivity at eBay but Couldn't Change Culture · Randy Shoup (eBay)
    Randy Shoup on doubling eBay engineering productivity via the DevOps playbook — and how a pathological, risk-averse culture with centralised waterfall planning blunted the gains and ultimately cost him his job.
  • 2026-06-02 · Building for Production · Liz Fong (Honeycomb)
    AI doesn't change the fundamentals — it amplifies whatever practices you already have; Honeycomb ships ~44% AI-authored changes by leaning harder on platform engineering, fast CI, continuous deployment, and closed-loop observability.
  • 2026-06-02 · State of AI in Software Development · DX — AI-Assisted Engineering Q1 Impact Report
    Insights across 400 orgs (50–10,000 engineers): 27.4% of code now AI-authored (up 8% from Q4), daily AI users ship 60% more PRs, dev ramp-up time nearly halved (~80 → ~30 days), and AI-readiness scorecards predict who absorbs the gains.

Reflections

  • 2026-06-03 · Platforms in an Increasingly Agentic World
    In an agentic world the middle layer disappears: clear-boundaried platforms, servers, documentation, domain expertise and generalists become the foundations — and identity is one of those platforms.
